definition: `SuccessivelyTemporal S x`: for some series i of the family S, x is present at an earlier and a later time of S i and its state differs between them. This is LifeHasSuccession of the q.10 duration frame (the negation of TotaSimul in DEF-BOETHIAN-ETERNAL) with presence in place of life. Being merely present at a time, or at several times without change of state, is not temporal in this sense.
note: The analyst's precisification of DEF-TEMPORAL-SUCCESSION-Q10 (time as the measure of change, with before and after, ST I q.10 a.4). It is relative to the supplied family: 'not temporal' means not successively temporal in any supplied series, not in every conceivable series. DISAMB-TEMPORAL-SENSE says how it treats Boethian eternity and the aevum. A source would be a passage that defines being in time as having a successive duration in this before/after sense.
